title: Register phone verbs (call, answer, hangup, text) and enforce is_device_active checks on text/message

sections.what: Register existing phone verbs (call, answer, hangup, text/message) in action_verbs.py, PlanGrounding, and contextual prompts, and make text/message verify is_device_active for both sender and recipient phones.
sections.why: routes/action_handlers.py (lines 1862-2009) and engine/long_distance_comms.py (lines 379-531) already implement call, answer, hangup, text, and message, yet none of those verbs are registered in engine/action_verbs.py (lines 64-160), PlanGrounding (lines 55-67), or contextual-actions.ts (lines 320-395). Furthermore, the text/message handler (lines 1902-2008) checks only 'phone' in name/tags without calling is_device_active, and writes an instant 'Received text' memory to the recipient even if the recipient owns no phone or has a dead battery.
sections.how: 1. Register 'call', 'answer', 'hangup', and 'text' (alias 'message') in engine/action_verbs.py and add them to PlanGrounding.PLAN_INTENT_ACTS.\n2. Surface phone verbs in contextual-actions.ts when carrying/near an active phone (including 'answer' / 'hangup' context when incoming_call_from or on_a_call).\n3. Update routes/action_handlers.py (lines 1900-2009) to reuse engine.long_distance_comms.is_device_active on the sender's device and verify recipient device activity for instant DM delivery/buzz notification (queuing unread messages until recipient phone is active rather than forcing immediate 'Saw/Received' awareness on an unpowered or uncarried device).
sections.verify: 1. Run pytest covering action_verbs registration and routes/action_handlers.py text/call/answer/hangup paths with powered vs dead/absent sender and recipient phones.\n2. Run npm run build:ts and node tools/unit/run.cjs verifying PlanGrounding and contextual-actions expose phone verbs when holding a phone or receiving a call.

acceptance.text: call, answer, hangup, and text (with message alias) are registered in engine/action_verbs.py, PlanGrounding.PLAN_INTENT_ACTS, and contextual-actions.ts when carrying or co-located with an active phone/comms device.
routes/action_handlers.py text/message handler validates is_device_active(world.graph, node) on sender's phone (refusing dead/powered-off devices) instead of matching only 'phone' in tags/name.

DM text/message checks whether the recipient has an active reachable phone before immediate delivery and records a subtle phone notification turn/sound event (unless silenced/off) rather than unconditionally writing a receipt memory into any powerless character.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Agent Turn Modal Available Actions & item brackets, plus Event Stream `[Call]` / text logs.

Current availability: routes/action_handlers.py (lines 1862-2009) and engine/long_distance_comms.py implement call/answer/hangup/text/message, but none are registered in action_verbs.py, plan-grounding.ts, or contextual-actions.ts, and text/message skips is_device_active checks on both sender and recipient.

Manual verification steps:
1. Give Character A an active phone and Character B either an active phone or a dead/powered-off phone.
2. Inspect A's Available Actions and send `text B hello` and `call B`.
   - expected: Phone verbs appear in contextual actions, dead phones cannot send or instantly receive messages, and active phones notify/deliver via Commons cleanly.
